_about: Every line of text the mod reads from a level file (level.text.<key>). halls.lua looks each one up with L("key", fallback). kind: lore = must rest on wiki facts (F ids); mechanic = must rest on how the mod plays (M ids); both = needs one of each. vars are placeholders that must stay in the line. needs: the line must cite at least one fact with one of these topics.

intro1.when: First subtitle. The elevator ride from Level 0 has just stopped early.

intro2.when: Second subtitle. The elevator doors open onto this level. First look at the place.

goal.when: Third subtitle. Says what the group has to do: find the tape, the valve and the fuse, then leave through the exit door.

huntWarn.when: Fourth subtitle. Warns what happens when the lights go out and where to go.

huntStart.when: The lights have just gone out and the hunt begins.

huntTaken.when: The lights go out because a player just picked up one of the three parts.

huntEnd.when: The lights come back and the hunt is over.

hudHunt.when: One or two words in capitals on the HUD while the lights are out.

refuge.when: Lights are out and every player is inside a room with a bed. The entity is not sent after them.

monsterNear.when: The room lamp stutters because the entity is close. {name} is the entity's name.

tipDeath.when: One-line tip on the death screen after the entity killed the player.

keyTaken.when: The player picked up the small key. {item} is its lower-case name.

doorShut.when: The player tried the exit door without all three parts. {parts} lists the missing ones.

doorOpen.when: The exit door takes the three parts and slides open.

exitSign.when: One word in capitals on the sign over the exit door. Also used in prompts: 'TRY THE <word> DOOR'. Not EXIT: untrustworthy EXIT signs already hang in the level. Take a word from the facts about the way out.

objectiveParts.when: Objective row in the game's overview: find the tape, the valve and the fuse.

objectiveKey.when: Objective row: find the small key.

objectiveExit.when: Objective row: leave through the exit door and the hall behind it. Should use the word from exitSign.

tipParts.when: One-line tip in the overview while parts are still missing. They lie on small tables in the rooms.

tipHall.when: One-line tip in the overview once the exit door is open: walk the hall and do not look back.

sealed.when: A trick: the doorway the player just came through is plain wall when they turn around.

chair.when: A trick: a wooden crate that stood against the wall has moved closer while nobody looked.

keyTurns.when: A trick: the locked door unlocks by itself as the player carrying the small key walks up.

noDoor.when: A trick: a doorway with an EXIT sign led into a dead-end passage. After the player walked back out it is plain wall, and this line shows when the player looks at it again.

hallSign.when: Capitals on a sign at the start of the long hall behind the exit door. Looking back there undoes progress.

hallEnter.when: The player steps into the long hall behind the exit door.

hallLook.when: The player looked back in the hall before making any progress.

hallLooked.when: The player looked back in the hall and lost the distance already walked.

hallPace.when: Part way down the hall. Something seems to follow.

hallSigns.when: Further down the hall. The EXIT signs overhead show a distance that is counting down.

hallLight.when: The end of the hall is finally in sight.

epiBig.when: Big capitals when the player reaches the room at the end of the hall.

epi1.when: First line in the small room at the end of the hall. It has one closed sliding door.

epi2.when: Second line in that room, just before the door's sign lights up with the name of the next level.

epiSign.when: Capitals on the sign over that door: the level this level's exit leads to according to the wiki, as 'LEVEL <number>'.

epiEnd.when: Big capitals as that door slides open. The floor is about to start over, so it should leave doubt.

epi3.when: The door stands open. Walking through starts the same floor again.

loop.when: The player walked through and is back in the first room. {n} is the loop number. Must start with 'LOOP {n}.'

whispers.when: Shown one at a time when a player has stood in the same room for 40 seconds. Quiet, unsettling observations about the place.
